about: A cozy idle game that lives in a narrow strip on the side of your screen. A herd of mountain goats climbs real peaks on its own while you work. Glance over, spend the metres they climb on more goats and surer footing, pass each camp, and summit the Seven Summits, from Kosciuszko to Everest.  A herd on the side of your screen          Ledge Goats lives in a tall, narrow strip on the left or right edge of your desktop. It stays on top, and clicks on the empty sky pass through to whatever is underneath. The goats hop from ledge to ledge by themselves. Look over whenever you like. There is always a goat doing something.  Look over, pick an upgrade, get back to work          Every metre a goat climbs is yours to spend. Every so often, spend it on one of six upgrades: more goats, faster climbing, steadier feet on rough rock, warm coats for wind and snow, calls that keep the herd moving in fog, or better grazing. It takes a click or two, and then you can look away again.  Camps, summits and the next mountain          Every peak has four camps on the way to the top. The first one, Kosciuszko, takes about a workday. The peaks get taller as you go, up to Everest, which takes about a working week. At each summit the herd settles on that mountain and you earn a permanent bonus. Then you start the next peak with a small new herd.  Five goats who come along for the whole trip          Most of the herd is just goats. Five of them have names, and once they join they come with you to every peak: the leader, the old one, the one with the rare coat and two more. Now and then one of them stops to do something goat-like, and the strip says so in a few words.  Weather slows them down. That's the worst of it.          Wind, fog and snow squalls slow the climb for a while, and clear days speed it up. Goats wobble and steady themselves. No goat is ever lost, and nothing you've earned is taken away. The herd climbs while the game is open and waits for you when it's closed.  Features    Seven real mountains, Kosciuszko to Everest, with four camps on each    Up to about 25 goats on screen at once, five of them named    Six upgrades, each levelled many times and bought in a click or two    Four kinds of weather that only slow the climb or speed it up    Coats, horns and bells to unlock at every camp and summit    An overlay mode with a transparent background, for stream layouts    Quiet by default, with music and sound licensed for streaming

name: TaskTown
lang: Korean
short: Turn your everyday clicks and keystrokes into in-game currency! Collect cute and stylish animals, help them find their tools, and build a peaceful village of your own.
about: Our Town Grows Even While You Work   Task Town is an  idle game  that turns the clicks and keystrokes made while using your computer into Town Coin, allowing you to rebuild and grow a quiet town together with its animal residents.  Keep the game open in a small window while you continue working or studying!  Even while you work, the residents use their assigned tools to help the town grow.         A New Chief Has Arrived—Bring Smiles Back to the Town!   A small town once filled with the laughter of animals has fallen silent.  As the newly appointed chief, you will collect Town Coin and welcome new residents and tools to the town.   Assign each resident a suitable tool and place them around the town to increase production.  As more residents arrive and the town level rises, new buildings and areas will be unlocked.   The once small and quiet town will gradually become lively again.            Game Highlights    Turn Your Everyday Inputs into In-Game Rewards   Earn Town Coin through mouse clicks and valid keyboard inputs while the game is running.  There is no need to focus on repetitive actions. Simply use your computer as usual and watch your town grow naturally.    49 Animal Residents and 40 Tools   Collect 49 animal residents with unique appearances and personalities, along with 40 different tools.  Animals and tools have their own grades and levels. Assigning a resident their designated tool grants a special production bonus.  Automatic Production Through Resident and Tool Combinations  Assign tools to the residents you have collected, and they will automatically produce Town Coin over time.  Consider which tool should be assigned to each resident, discover more efficient combinations, and create your own production structure.     A Little Town That Stays with You on Your Desktop   Task Town allows you to keep your town visible on the screen while using other programs.  Clicks pass through transparent areas that contain no game elements, allowing you to interact with your desktop. You can also freely switch between compact and expanded views whenever needed.     New Challenges After Rebuilding the Town   After fully rebuilding the town, you can either remain in your current town and continue growing or begin a new run at a higher difficulty.  Take on Normal, Hard, and VeryHard difficulties to discover new residents and collectibles.        How to Play   Click and type → Earn Town Coin → Draw animals and tools → Assign tools to residents → Automatic production   → Upgrade growth elements → Increase the town level → Rebuild the town    Collect Town Coin by clicking and typing.    Spend coins to draw animal residents and tools.    Assign suitable tools to your residents.    Place your chosen residents around the town.    Collect automatic production and input rewards to upgrade growth elements.     Basic Controls     Left and right mouse clicks: Earn Town Coin    Keyboard input: Earn Town Coin from valid inputs    Left-click UI elements: Use the draw, inventory, collection, placement, and upgrade menus    Drag the town: Move the town’s position in expanded view    Click an animal resident: Enlarge the selected resident and have the camera follow them    Click an empty area: Stop the camera from following the resident    Compact/Expand button: Switch between the small desktop view and the full town view          Recommended For Players Who     Want a game they can keep open while working or studying    Enjoy cute animal characters and charming miniature towns    Like idle games featuring collection, combinations, and automatic production    Enjoy the sense of accomplishment that comes from watching a town grow little by little    Like experimenting with their own resident and tool combinations       Developer’s Comment   Task Town began as a project designed to create an experience where everyday life contributes to the growth of an in-game town, rather than requiring players to stop what they are doing to play.    We wa

name: Pocket Partner
lang: English*, Japanese**
short: A lightweight, fully customizable desktop companion. Bring 3D anime characters to your screen with full VRM support. Experience unprecedented control: import your own animations, edit materials, change facial expressions, save custom outfits, and interact with physics while you work or play.
about: Pocket Partner is a lightweight desktop companion that brings 3D avatars to life on your screen. While other desktop pets lock you into preset behaviors, Pocket Partner is built entirely around deep, granular customization. Import your favorite .vrm models, build personalized outfits, and completely overhaul the animations and audio to make your partner your own.     COMPLETE CUSTOMIZATION           Go far beyond just loading a model. Pocket Partner gives you direct control over your avatar's appearance and state right on your desktop.     The Outfit System:  Save your edits and instantly swap between customized looks on the fly.     Mesh & Material Editing:  Toggle specific clothing meshes on or off and swap materials using built-in preset shaders.     Advanced Blendshapes:  Trigger facial expressions and blendshapes, and bind them directly to specific animations for unique reactions.      BRING YOUR OWN ANIMATIONS & AUDIO          Don't like the default idle pose? Change it. Pocket Partner allows you to import your own custom animations and swap them out in real time. You can also replace any built-in sound effect with your own custom audio files.    Assign your custom imports (or use the built-in defaults) to a variety of dynamic states:     Intro & Idle:  Welcomes you on startup and breathes life into your desktop.     AFK / Sleep:  Dozes off when you step away from your PC.     Drag:  Pick up your partner and drag them around.     Window Sitting:  Snaps to the top of your active windows or taskbar to watch you work.     Edge Hiding:  Watch your partner peek out from the left or right edge of your monitor.     Manual Triggers:  Command your partner to dance, wave, or perform any imported animation on demand.      TACTILE & INTERACTIVE          Your partner reacts dynamically to your cursor. Pick them up and drag them across your screen with dedicated dragging animations, or engage with them directly:     Hand Holding:  Move your cursor near their hands and watch them reach out to catch it. Don't fall in love.     Head & Spine Tracking:  Your partner will watch and track your cursor from anywhere on the screen.     Hair Flicking & Physics:  Full interactive springbone support means hair, skirts, and accessories flick, bounce, and sway naturally when you run your mouse over them.       A Note on Importing:   The app natively supports standard .vrm models and .fbx animation files. Physics, animations, materials and clipping quality will depend on how the original artist rigged the imported model.

about: Write your manifesto with a friend.   Eldon Desktop Buddy puts Eldon and his friends on your desktop. They hang around while you work, react when you click them, and occasionally get on with something of their own. Drag them somewhere useful. Or somewhere annoying.  It's a free desktop toy with a cast of voiced, animated characters, three games, and a few other things to distract you. Keep the ball moving and put your score on the online board.   PeeBitties Mania  Guide Eldon through a platforming adventure. Jump, fly, steer your spells and collect PeeBitties. Online, you can duel other players, use the live chat wall, send private mail and read the Gazette. Your progress saves as you play, and the forest gives you fresh fights each day. name: Cursor Cult Demo
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: Play the Stone Age of Cursor Cult. A tiny pixel tribe lives on an island at the edge of your screen and worships your mouse cursor. Every 20 seconds its priests read your cursor's trail as an omen: farm, build, trade, pray, study, or march to war. Lead them to the dawn of the Bronze Age.
about: Your cursor is their god This free demo is the Stone Age of Cursor Cult, a desktop companion. A tiny pixel-art island docks along the edge of your screen, and two tribes live on it, one at each end. They worship the Sky Hand: your mouse cursor. Every 20 seconds their priests read the trail your cursor left behind as an omen, and steer the tribe by it.  You never have to play it. Just use your computer, and your everyday mouse habits become the tribe's scripture. When you feel like it, gesture on purpose: draw circles, shake the cursor, or rest it over the island. Read the omens    The Great Wheel  (circles): farming, more fields and farmers    The Pillar of Heaven  (long vertical strokes): industry, lumber camps and quarries    The Long Road  (long horizontal strokes): trade, markets and merchants    The Storm of Wrath  (frantic shaking): arms; relations sour, and war may follow    The Gentle Breeze  (slow, gentle wandering): peace    The Gaze of the Sky  (resting over the island): faith, temples and priests    The Dance of Stars  (moving along the far edge of the screen): learning, libraries and scholars    The Silence  (not moving): nothing changes, and long silences make the people uneasy  An omen guide in your tribe's panel tracks which of the eight you have found. What's in the demo   The whole Stone Age: huts, fields, lumber camps, quarries, markets, temples, libraries, fishing boats and war canoes.   Lead one tribe, the other, or both. Each tribe hears only its own half of the screen.   Relations drift with your omens, and wars of clubs and headbands break out and end in peace.   Hover still over villagers and they kneel in awe. Shake the cursor over a village to call down lightning.   The demo ends when your tribe is ready for the Bronze Age. The full game carries on through Bronze, Iron, Kingdoms and the Industrial Age, with ships, aircraft and buildings that change with every age.   Made to sit on your desktop all day   Transparent and always on top. Clicks pass through everywhere except the island itself.   Dock it to the bottom, top, left or right edge. Pick its size, or hide the panels.   Quiet, restrained sound. Turn it off at any time.   English and Simplified Chinese.

name: Desktop Party: An Idle Fantasy RPG Demo
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Arabic, Bulgarian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Romanian, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish - Latin America, Swedish, Thai, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese
short: A tiny party lives on your desktop in this idle RPG. Your heroes fight monsters and find treasure while you work or browse. Choose their gear and watch them grow into new forms. Take a break to pet them or play with toys. Sometimes it rains frogs.
about: Your party travels through forests, ruins and snowy paths along the edge of your screen. They fight the monsters they meet and collect treasure as they go. You choose who joins the party and how they are equipped.  A life between battles                  After a few battles, your heroes set up camp. They share food, sort their treasure and act out stories for each other. When they are ready, they pack up and carry on.  Watch them grow          As your heroes learn their professions, they earn new forms and tools. You choose which looks each hero wears, and earlier forms stay available. After completing a world, you can take the party into a new one, keeping your heroes, gear and collection. Completed worlds also earn trophies to display beside the party.  Build your party          Discover eight professions and choose a role for each hero. Some attack while others guard or heal. Their spells and equipment change how they fight, so you can try new combinations as your collection grows. The battles play themselves.  Pick them up and play          Pet a hero, give them a toss or throw a paper glider for them to chase. Toys bounce and spin around the party. Frogs and treasure chests can fall from above, landing among your heroes as they react.          Make room on your desktop  Put the party along the bottom or side of your screen and change its size to suit your desktop. Click through empty space to use the programs behind it. A hotkey switches on gaming mode so the whole game ignores the mouse.  Your day can help them grow  Optional activity sensing lets your daily computer use help matching heroes grow. Coding helps the Rune Coder, writing helps the Quill Knight, and typing can speed up battles. All sensing stays on your PC. The game never records what you type. You can switch sensing off and unlock every profession through adventure.  Come back when you like  Chests open themselves and gear is sorted for you. If the party loses a battle, they recover on safer ground and keep going. They can earn progress while the game is closed, with a summary waiting when you return. A weekly pixel card records their adventures for you to save and share.

name: Writelings
lang: English
short: A small illustrated writer sits in the corner of your screen and works on a book of their own, but only while you type. Their published books pay out ink you can spend on new writers. Writelings counts your keystrokes and never records which keys.
about: A writer on your desktop  Writelings is a desktop companion for Windows. A small illustrated writer sits at a desk in a corner of your screen, on top of whatever you're writing in: Word, Google Docs, an email, code, anything.  They're working on a book of their own, and they only write while you type. Stop, and they look up and think for a while before they doze off. Start typing again and so do they. They can't write their masterpiece without you.  Books and ink  Books come in sizes, from a 500-word short story to tomes that run into the millions of words. When your writer finishes one, it goes on their shelf and pays royalties in ink. The whole backlist keeps paying, including for several hours after you close the app.  Writers  You start with the Night Owl, who writes at a lamp-lit desk under the stars. Ink buys new writers, and the cast keeps growing. Each one comes with a whole lit scene of their own:    A frog wizard on a lily pad under a paper lantern    A raftsman on the Mississippi before dawn    A Victorian postmaster mouse working by a thimble of candlelight    A tortoise writing in a glasshouse in flat daylight    A small cloud in a beret, writing the weather into an almanac    A pink slime in a dungeon, writing up the adventurers he ate. He's lit from the inside by the wizard's crystal he swallowed. His desk is a shield on a sword and his pen is an arrow.    Some of them quote their favorite authors while they work. Two stay locked until you've written 80,000 words of your own.  Staying out of the way  Clicks pass through the writer to whatever is underneath. Drag them anywhere and resize them. The panel above them holds their current book, your stats, the shelf, and the shop. It comes in different interface skins, dark and light, so you can pick whichever works best on your screen. Hide it and it's just the writer at their desk.  How it knows you're typing  Windows tells Writelings each time a key goes down, and Writelings adds one to a count. That count is the only input.    It never records which key was pressed, so your words are never read or stored.    It doesn't look at which program or window you're in, or what your documents are called.    Nothing about your typing leaves your computer. There are no analytics and no telemetry.    There are no accounts and no launcher, and nothing runs online. Your progress is one save file on your own computer. Writelings is built with Electron, so its code ships readable in the install folder if you want to check.

name: Desk Hive
lang: English**
short: Tend a living beehive right on your desk. Harvest honey through the seasons, expand your apiary, build a processing line, and automate the work while you're away. A cozy idle beekeeping sim that runs beside you.
about: Desk Hive is a gentle idle beekeeping sim that lives on your desktop while you do other things. You start with one hive, a smoker, and some bees. Over time you grow more colonies, upgrade your equipment, and slowly automate the whole operation. The bees keep working when you close the game.  Gameplay  Each hive runs in real time. Workers forage, honey fills up the supers, and new bees hatch from brood frames. Every colony has a queen with her own traits that affect how fast the hive grows and how much honey it makes. You can upgrade brood boxes to raise worker capacity, install more frames to improve efficiency, and keep sugar feed stocked so the bees don't starve when winter arrives.  Seasons change every six hours whether you're playing or not. Spring is good for building up your workforce. Summer brings the strongest nectar flow. Autumn slows everything down and it's your last chance to stock supplies. Winter is harsh: nectar drops to nearly nothing, brood production grinds to a halt, and every hive burns through sugar feed just to stay alive. A full year cycles in 24 real hours.          The production chain  When a honey super is full, you use the smoker to calm the hive, harvest the frames, and queue extractor jobs to spin raw honey into bulk product. Better extractors process bigger batches and run more jobs at once. Once you own two hives, you unlock jarring stations that package bulk honey into jars worth a lot more money. Sell the jars, sell the wax, reinvest in your apiary.  Upgrades come in three tiers: brood boxes for colony size, extractors for processing speed, and jarring stations for packaging throughput. You can also add more honey supers per hive and install extra brood frames to squeeze out more efficiency.          Automation  Seven automation upgrades let you step back from the busywork as your apiary grows. Auto smoke keeps harvest ready hives calm. Extractor loader harvests and queues extraction jobs on its own. Collector tray grabs finished extractor output. Sales contract sells off excess honey when storage gets full. Supply clerk restocks jars and sugar feed at thresholds you set. Jar line assistant keeps packaging batches running. Apiary supervisor extends everything across hives you're not currently watching.  Offline progress  Close the game and everything keeps running. The simulation covers up to 36 real hours while you're gone, the first 12 at full speed and then gradually slower. When you come back you get a summary of what your bees made: honey produced, jars filled, wax collected, money earned, jobs finished.  No pressure  There's no fail state. If you forget to stock sugar feed before winter, your colonies just slow way down. They don't die. Check in when you feel like it, queue up some jobs, tweak your automation, and let the bees do the rest.

about: A medieval village on a floating island that lives in the corner of your desktop.   Hoverwick is a cozy game about building and decorating a village. You work, read or watch a film, and right next to you the villagers bake bread, go fishing and build snowmen. One click and you're in the village, another and you're back to your day.          The island floats above your desktop without taking over your screen. Click the empty sky next to it and you land right back in the program you were using.   Clicks next to the island go through to the windows underneath   Place the island anywhere on your screen   Tuck the whole village into a small bubble with one shortcut   On Windows, the island slips behind full-screen games and films on its own   The village keeps working even when the game is closed   Prefer a regular game? Hoverwick also runs in a window and in full screen              You choose the spot for every house, workshop and field, and when the village grows you can move them for free. Grain goes to the mill, flour to the bakery, and the production chains carry on across new islands, all the way to the most refined goods.   162 buildings and 184 goods linked into production chains   50 manor levels, and buildings change their look up to 10 times   Move buildings for free and upgrade several levels at once   Over 100 research projects at the merchants' guild and on the islands   Trade and production rules that sell your surplus and switch workshops for you              The season changes with every real day, while the village keeps its own clock, from dawn to starry night.   Spring, summer, autumn and winter change the colours of the whole island   Rain, downpours, thunderstorms, fog and windy days   Puddles after the rain, drips from the roofs and a frozen river in winter   Lamps light up at dusk, and fireflies circle the island at night   Lock the season, time of day and weather just the way you like them              The villagers aren't just scenery. Each has a name and a job, and in their free time they pick one of over 70 pastimes, depending on the season, the time of day and the weather.   In winter they skate on the frozen river, go on sleigh rides, build snowmen and fish through holes in the ice   In autumn they go mushroom picking, in summer they play on the swings, and at night they watch the stars   They ask you for small favours, become your friends and sometimes chat with you while you work   Follow any villager step by step and watch their day up close   Pick up farm animals with your mouse and carry them wherever you like. Throw one off the island and it always comes back in its own way: the cow in a superhero cape, the pig on angel wings, the rabbit riding a carrot rocket              You paint paths and water with a brush, so they run exactly where your hand leads them. Bring a stream to the edge of the island and it tumbles off as a waterfall.   18 path surfaces, from packed earth to marble   Water, lava, honey, acid and tar, each with its own waterfalls. Winter changes each of them differently: water freezes, lava cools into obsidian, honey crystallises, tar thickens and acid steams          Bridges fit themselves to the water beneath them, and fences follow your cursor in any shape.   A low footbridge over a trickle, a tall bridge over a river   Bridges of wood, stone, brick and marble, just like the paths   Fences, walls and hedges with gates, on the grid or completely freehand          Put decorations wherever you want: on the ground, on roofs, on walls, and even stack crates and barrels on top of each other.   Over 150 decorations in many colours and sizes   Sow flowers with a scatter brush   Give every island its own roof colour, ground and cliff rock   Copy a decorated corner as a blueprint, paste it somewhere else or send it to friends as a code   Undo any mistake with one shortcut          Once the village has grown, the lighthouse sends expeditions to new islands. You build it however you want, add creatures and inhabitants then watch it grow and flourish while you use your computer and go about your day. Pop in whenever you want to see how things are evolving and experience your cozy world from the first person view of any inhabitant you want!               What's in the box:     THE TINY DESKTOP TERRARIUM OF YOUR DREAMS!    Lots of cool stuff (like sand, sand is cool) you get to pour and toss wherever you like to build your terrarium. If you can dream it, you can build a terrarium of it!    The terrarium is designed to sit on your desktop wherever you like it. It sits on top of your other windows so you can always see it. about: Galacto is a cozy idle game you keep at the bottom of your screen. Ships pull in for fuel, bots do the work, and you collect the money, slowly turning one working pump into the busiest gas station in the galaxy!                      A ship docks. A bot walks over and starts the pump. When it's done, you click to get paid. That's the whole loop, and it's weirdly hard to stop doing. It plays itself while you're busy. It pays out when you're not.                    Buy more pumps. Hire more bots to run them. Upgrade your pumps and gear at Tony's Garage so every ship pays out more. The whole place gets busier, louder, and more alive with every credit you sink into it.                  Hit one button and the whole game folds into a tiny icon you can park anywhere on your screen. It keeps running underneath, ships refuel, creds stack up, nothing pauses. Click the icon and it slides right back.                  Collect ships fast enough and they chain into a combo. Since ships never leave and money never expires, a row of them sitting there isn't a backlog, it's a combo waiting to happen. Step away, let them stack up, then come back and clear the whole line in one window. Stepping away isn't punished here. It's how you set up the big one. about: Myriad: Radiant Frontlines is a  free-to-play idle RPG  that fits in a corner of your desktop.  Join Joan of Arc and recruit 30 adult heroines from history and mythology around the world. Build your team, equip them and challenge six mythic bosses. Between battles, give gifts to your favorites, grow closer to them and collect their artwork. Keep them nearby while you work. Open up the battle when you're free.  Keep a small battle window in a corner of your desktop while you work or study. Your heroines fight automatically. Check in on the action, their expressions and their little remarks whenever you like.  When you have time, expand the battlefield to watch them take on a boss, or open your team and try a different lineup. Switch between the two window sizes while the battle continues. Raise your favorite heroines and build your team  Each heroine has her own skills and traits. Collect heroines and fragments, develop your favorites, unlock skills and choose their order of entry.  Up to three heroines fight at once, with reserves joining in turn. You decide who goes first, who deals damage and who provides protection or healing. Assemble your team and let them fight. Challenge mythic bosses and upgrade your gear  Fight bosses for equipment and growth materials. Find suitable weapons for your heroines, compare random affixes, enhance their gear and take on tougher stages.  Stuck on a stage? Try a different lineup, or farm gear and develop your heroines before coming back. Fight together, give gifts and collect their artwork  Fight alongside your favorites and give them gifts they like. Raise affinity to unlock illustrations in their Affinity Albums.  Separate Private Albums feature them in different outfits and settings. Revisit any picture you've collected and gradually complete your favorites' collections. A 25-minute focus timer with rewards  Start a 25-minute Pomodoro timer when you need to focus on work or study.  Battles pause during focus time while materials and gifts accumulate. Finish the timer, collect your rewards and return to your adventure. Free to play, with offline play  The base game is free. Keep battling and developing your heroines without an internet connection. Progress is saved locally. A note from the developer  Hi! I'm the developer of Myriad: Radiant Frontlines, and I'm new to game development, learning as I go.  I wanted a game I'd happily keep running on my desktop: let the heroines fight while I'm busy, then spend my free time trying team setups, farming equipment, giving gifts to my favorites and collecting nice artwork.  That's how Myriad came about.  I've used a lot of AI assistance in creating and developing this game. You could call it my experiment in "AI overdrive": try an idea, throw it out if it doesn't work, and learn along the way. AI has helped me make things I could only imagine before, then keep revising them until I'm happy with them.  There's still plenty to improve. If you find bugs, stuttering, confusing controls or a stage that feels unfair, please tell me in the Steam community. Screenshots and a description of what you were doing make it easier to track down the problem.   I'll keep fixing bugs, prioritizing issues that block play, damage saves or leave rewards missing. I'll explain the fixes in the update notes.   I'll also keep adding artwork, improving animations and skill effects, and adjusting progression. Let me know your favorite heroines, outfits or settings you'd like to see, or anything that's bothering you.  Thanks for checking out my game. I hope you have fun and find a heroine you love. about: Your desktop has a new neighbour Gramps & Whiskers is a desktop companion. A grumpy old fisherman settles down on your Windows taskbar, casts his line and keeps you company while you work, browse or play. His ginger cat roams your desktop: it hops onto your windows, hangs from their edges, climbs their sides and keeps a close eye on grandpa's bucket. What happens on your desktop   Grandpa fishes on the taskbar: bites, catches, the odd old boot and plenty of grumbling.   The cat lives on your windows: it walks along their tops, climbs up their sides and rides along when you drag them around.   Step away from the computer and grandpa dozes off. The cat may curl up on his lap.   Leave the bucket unattended and the cat will steal a fish. Grandpa will notice.   Grandpa comments on what you have open: videos, music, code, chats and more.   Grandpa's catch: now and then he reels in a cosmetic item instead of a fish — hats, scarves, collars, glasses and fishing gear. Items come in five rarities, from Common to Legendary, and go straight to your Steam Inventory.   The game is free, with nothing to buy.   Pick the cat up by the scruff and drop it anywhere. Everywhere else your clicks go straight through, so they never get in your way.   Lightweight, lives in the system tray, 19 languages.   Privacy To comment on what you are doing, grandpa looks only at the name of the active program and its window title. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere, and you can switch it off in the tray menu.

name: Desktop Companion - Asiden
lang: English**
short: Meet your AI desktop companion. Chat by voice or text, play games together, or let them watch along as you play. about: Please come and join my discord  to give feedback and ask for support. That is where I can help you the fastest. A little company. A lot of control. A familiar face on your desktop. A conversation while you play. Someone who remembers the interview you were nervous about and asks how it went.  Asiden is a talking AI desktop companion with personality, memory and optional screen awareness. Chat by text or microphone, play a game together, or let your companion watch along and comment as you play your own games. You choose when they can see your screen and how often they speak, whether you want lively company or a quieter presence while you get on with your day.   Buy once for local AI on compatible hardware. No per-message charges for local use. Optional cloud features cost extra.       Find your kind of company Meet Mika, Lily and Sasha in expressive Live2D, alongside Asiden's included 3D companions.    Mika:  cheeky, curious and playful, with a caring side beneath the occasional pout.    Lily:  gentle, warm and encouraging, with plenty of room for excitement.    Sasha:  sharp, teasing and a little smug. Expect a comeback.  Choose a companion, create your own personality, or import a compatible VRM avatar. Your choice of appearance, personality and memories are distinct: changing a look does not mean starting your memories again. Mika's signature personality belongs to her Live2D model; her look can also be used with another personality.      Remembers what matters. You stay in control. Your interests, the people in your life, something you were looking forward to: your companion can bring relevant details back into conversation without you repeating the whole story.  Open Memory to see the saved notes.  Edit a mistake, update something that has changed, or delete an entry you do not want kept.  Things you have told your companion are shown separately from things they have inferred. AI can get things wrong; the saved entries shown here are yours to review and correct.      A little friendly competition Play  Secret Guest , Asiden's first built-in companion game. Pick a secret face, ask about visible traits and narrow down the board before your companion guesses yours.  Watch the cards go down as you play, trade a little banter between turns, and return later to finish the same game. Its conversation stays with the game, separate from your everyday chat.      Make conversation fit your day    Short replies or longer conversations:  adjust how much room your companion has to respond.    Quiet company or a chatty companion:  choose how often they speak first, or use Quiet Mode to stop proactive conversation.    A voice and a face:  hear spoken replies with expressive character movement, or keep things text-only.    Your desktop, your style:  customise appearance, window colour, transparency and text size.  Pause when you need to step away: conversation, speech, microphone input and proactive screen activity stop together. Share what you are looking at Ask about something on your screen, allow occasional glances, or draw a box around one area to discuss. Screen awareness is optional, with controls for when and where your companion looks.  For supported games, download knowledge packs to give conversations more context about their worlds, mechanics and terminology. Packs are stored locally after download. Local AI included. Cloud is your choice. Run chat, voice, speech recognition, screen vision and memory on compatible hardware. After initial setup and the required model downloads, installed local features can work with Steam in Offline Mode. No separate Asiden account is required for local use. Local conversations and memories stay on your PC.  Optional cloud chat, vision and voices use  prepaid Sparks through Steam Wallet . No subscription, automatic renewal or automatic top-up. about: Click And Slash     Click and Slash is a desktop clicker: get your everyday tasks done while staying productive. You’ll be able to track your number of clicks per day, week, and month, along with a percentage that evaluates your productivity accordingly.  Perfect for forcing yourself to get some work done! But don’t forget to upgrade your damage and make the cutest monsters in your area tremble in fear.  You can even be AFK at your computer and still keep making monsters suffer. That’s right: you can deal damage without clicking, while sitting back and watching your life slowly pass before your eyes.  Fill up your encyclopedia with cute, absurd monsters, all lovingly tortured by you. You’re such a nice person...  So, you know what you have to do, right?                    --- Gameplay ---  Click and Slash is designed to fit right into your everyday life, on your glorious PC Master Race! No need to buy ridiculously expensive RAM just to play: even the tiniest setup will do! In this game, you’ll face cute monsters who want only one thing: violence! Your goal is to beat them up and make some cash.     Click:  Everything is tracked: your number of clicks is recorded whether it’s for the day, the month, or even the year! Prestige:  Reset your monsters’ health to 0 and face them with increased power, as if you had somehow gained muscles without doing any exercise.     Info & Productivity:  It’s all in the details. And don’t worry: no chest here will ever make you lose your precious click count! You’ll also be able to discover the monster’s details and its story, no matter how ridiculous it may be.     Options:  So yes, like in every game, you have options... exciting, right? You can turn on some background music, listen to the monster’s sound when you hit it, and even... when you kill it!     Cowork:  Like having your interface right there with you? Create your own to-do list, where you can set all your goals or write down the Christmas presents you never got... what a sad life.     Quests:  To make absolutely sure you’re working, we’ve prepared plenty of quests for you!     LightMod:  Want to reduce the size of your game interface? Just click your mouse wheel to shrink the interface and make the most of your workspace.     Conclusion:  We make your work count by tracking everything you do. Become productive while fighting the cute monsters that accompany you. Optimize your damage and gold, and upgrade your abilities.       And above all… live your life. Or what’s left of it. It won’t block your clicks, so you can keep using your computer while he cuts through enemies.           YOU WORK. HE FIGHTS.   Enemies attack from all four sides, and your fighter automatically strikes back. Chests drop, loot piles up, and your character grows stronger. Even while the game is closed, you’ll continue earning Coins and XP for up to 8 hours.           LOOT. MERGE. GROW STRONGER.   More than 5,900 items and 10 rarity tiers await. about: Here, pigeons. Dinner's served.  Ever wanted to catch a pigeon?  So we made this. The last place in South Korea where you can feed pigeons as much as you like.    It's  your desktop  (in Overlay mode).          GuGuGuGu   Pigeon Idle : GuGuGuGu  is an   idle pigeon-catching game  .  The controls are simple.     Left click: scatter breadcrumbs.            Right click: swing your bug net.         The busier a pigeon is eating, the easier it is to catch. Miss, and every pigeon nearby gets spooked and flies off too.       Your time is precious. Turn the money from selling pigeons into automated pigeon income.  Upgrade your feed, bug net, traps, and automation equipment in the  shop . From your second run,  Auto upgrade  buys the next levels for you along the route you pick.       Rumor has it that a pigeon you set free might come back to repay the favor... But can you resist once you catch a whiff of rotisserie pigeon?            Release enough of them and something good might happen.       Or sell enough "rotisserie chicken" and you might end up in some ugly trouble.     Either way, neither one is illegal.    Pigeon-Powered Product Development  Sell pigeons to the Beauty Lab to earn experiment samples. Stop the five reagent tubes one by one, match the pictures, and create new pigeon cosmetics.          Pigeon Express 999  Save up for a migration ticket and you move to the next neighborhood.  From the banks of the Han River all the way to heaven.   9    neighborhoods, each home to  9  pigeon species .  What  adventures   pigeons  await you?          Raising Free-Range Pigeons  Press the  Pigeon Mode  button and the game screen disappears, leaving only pigeons strolling along the bottom of your screen. Pick  up to  9  favorites from every pigeon you've met  and let them roam free.       Pick no favorites, and one lonely pigeon wanders around.          Click any pigeon to return to the game.    The pigeons will remember this  Did you know  a pigeon's IQ is  9+9  ? I didn't.  Pigeons remember what you do. Like whether you smell of rotisserie chicken or not...           Finish a run and you earn  24   GG  points (GuGu points) . Spend them on the 722 nodes of the  GG Upgrade Tree , 1 GG per node, and start your next run a little easier. about: "Akari: Lovely Moments with You" is a heartwarming desktop companion game. As a spin-off of the mystery ADV "The Night the Star Fell," this title focuses on the daily life between the player and the heroine—Shinonome Akari.  Here, you can take a break from the heavy suspense and riddles of the original game, build the bridge between dimensions, and spend every ordinary yet sparkling day with this gentle sister. Whether it's her quiet presence while you work or intimate interactions during your leisure time, your "best of times" is quietly beginning...          Enter a Focus State Together   Features a built-in Pomodoro timer. When you turn on Focus Mode, Akari will also quietly open a book on your desktop, joining you in your study or work session. Completing each focus cycle not only boosts your productivity but also earns you precious "Inspiration" points, helping Akari’s Inspiration level grow and unlocking more bonds between you.   Immersive Companionship   Through daily clicks and interactions, every moment spent together turns into "Inspiration Fragments." In the in-game exchange shop, you can use your points to unlock more beautiful outfits, diverse desktop wallpapers and soothing background music. As your Inspiration level increases, more exclusive content will become available.   Lightweight Desktop Interaction   You can place Akari anywhere on your screen and define her movement area. Whether you're writing, drawing, or binge-watching shows, Akari will stay by your side in the most comfortable way—never in the way, but always there for you.   Discover Everything About Her Where Reality and Fantasy Meet   In the game, you'll experience both real daily life with Akari and perhaps see a side of her she’s never shown before (born from your own imagination). Collect high-quality illustrations created by talented artists and fully experience her charm!         This title is closely linked to the developer's upcoming game "The Night the Star Fell." While waiting for the main game's release, you might discover some hidden easter eggs related to the original story right here in your desktop companion...

short: A tiny party lives on your desktop in this idle RPG. Your heroes fight monsters and find treasure while you work or browse. Choose their gear and watch them grow into new forms. Take a break to pet them or play with toys. Sometimes it rains frogs.
about: Your party travels through forests, ruins and snowy paths along the edge of your screen. They fight the monsters they meet and collect treasure as they go. You choose who joins the party and how they are equipped.  A life between battles                  After a few battles, your heroes set up camp. They share food, sort their treasure and act out stories for each other. When they are ready, they pack up and carry on.  Watch them grow          As your heroes learn their professions, they earn new forms and tools. You choose which looks each hero wears, and earlier forms stay available. After completing a world, you can take the party into a new one, keeping your heroes, gear and collection. Completed worlds also earn trophies to display beside the party.  Build your party          Discover eight professions and choose a role for each hero. Some attack while others guard or heal. Their spells and equipment change how they fight, so you can try new combinations as your collection grows. The battles play themselves.  Pick them up and play          Pet a hero, give them a toss or throw a paper glider for them to chase. Toys bounce and spin around the party. Frogs and treasure chests can fall from above, landing among your heroes as they react.          Make room on your desktop  Put the party along the bottom or side of your screen and change its size to suit your desktop. Click through empty space to use the programs behind it. A hotkey switches on gaming mode so the whole game ignores the mouse.  Your day can help them grow  Optional activity sensing lets your daily computer use help matching heroes grow. Coding helps the Rune Coder, writing helps the Quill Knight, and typing can speed up battles. All sensing stays on your PC. The game never records what you type. You can switch sensing off and unlock every profession through adventure.  Come back when you like  Chests open themselves and gear is sorted for you. If the party loses a battle, they recover on safer ground and keep going. They can earn progress while the game is closed, with a summary waiting when you return. A weekly pixel card records their adventures for you to save and share.

lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese
short: Nothing beats a company-paid holiday! Perfect attendance earned you an unlimited vacation—100% savings on hotels and restaurants, because there are none. Give up and crawl back to work, or survive the wild. A cozy desktop idle survival game. Endure your way to the top.
about: [MEMO: TO ALL VACATIONING EMPLOYEES]     Congratulations on your Perfect Attendance Award. Please read the following notice carefully.     1. Please Enjoy Your Vacation at Your Desk     Chief Endurance Officer is a semi-automatic wilderness survival game that lives quietly in the corner of your work screen. Eight hours at the office equals five full days in the wild. You only need to make a few key decisions during work breaks: Where to explore today? Reinforce the camp? What tools to craft?—The rest of the time, your character will do the hard work for you.     2. Pins Are Distributed According to Labor—Eat More, Earn More     Pins are your action points in the wilderness. Each morning, use pins to plan your day: up to three, one each for morning, midday, and afternoon. Where do pins come from? From last night's dinner—want to get more done tomorrow? Eat more tonight.     3. A Destination You Can Trust     First stop: the mountains of Guangzhou, China. You will be staying in a panoramic eco-suite, with all ingredients freshly caught and gathered, unlimited servings—every plant and animal is drawn from reality, researched and verified one by one.    The more you know about real-world materials and bushcraft, the better tools you'll craft and the more "surprise events" you'll survive. And if you know absolutely nothing about the outdoors? No worries—a few missed meals and you'll figure it out.     4. Diversified Performance Reviews     The longer you endure, the closer you get to the legendary title of Chief Endurance Officer. Of course, endurance isn't everything. The company encourages well-rounded development: Chief Casualty Officer, Chief Starvation Officer, Chief Toxicology Officer, Chief Electrocution Officer—welcome to the C-suite.     5. Team Building Is Permitted     You may invite up to four friends to "vacation" together. Most days, you'll each be enduring on your own; when your paths cross, take a photo, trade journals. And in a true emergency, you may send out a distress call—after all, hard times reveal true friends.    The company reserves the right of final interpretation of this notice. Enjoy your vacation.

about: THE APOCALYPSE FITS IN A STRIP ABOVE YOUR TASKBAR  Idle of the Dead is a zombie-apocalypse idle RPG that runs in Windows taskbar. Your squad auto-battles endless zombie hordes while you work, browse, or play something else, and it keeps earning even while you're offline.            LEAD A SQUAD OF SURVIVORS  Command the bat-swinging Outlaw, the sharpshooting Scout and the life-saving Nurse. They attack, dodge, heal and unleash skills automatically, you build the team and the team clears the horde.            A LOT OF CONTENT TO EXPLORE  Four escalating difficulties (Outbreak, Collapse, Extermination, Apocalypse), each with 3 Acts and dozens of stages. A dozen hand-drawn biomes, from ruined suburbs to the burning depths of hell, with elite mini-bosses and a towering boss in every Act.            DEEP PROGRESSION  Eight gear slots on every survivor, plus a skill tree with dozens of talents to build around. Swap heroes and rebuild the squad whenever a run stops working. Reach level 100 and prestige opens, with super-prestige sitting behind it.            LOOT & RARITY  Hunt gear across nine rarities, from common junk all the way up to Patient Zero. Eight stash tabs to fill, sockets and sets to line up, and a perfect roll that never quite shows up.            DDTANK-STYLE FORGE (0 TO +15)  Push your weapons up with gold and stones. Luck stones raise your odds, protection stones hold your level, and from +11 on a failed attempt destroys the item unless a protection stone is riding along.            THE SYNTHESIS TERMINAL  Nine items of the same rarity and category go in, one of the next rarity up comes out. Auto-fill picks them for you, and the same workshop also crafts, recycles, engraves and rerolls what you already own.            ASYNCHRONOUS PVP  Challenge another survivor's build and watch the fight play out. Nobody has to be online. Training pits you against a mirror of your own squad, the Daily Raid gives you three legs and two losses to spend, and the Top 100 tells you where you actually stand.                  YOUR LOOT IS REAL STEAM ITEMS  Unique drops become tradable items in your Steam Inventory. The Convoy ships them out of the game, and from there you list them, sell them, or buy what someone else pulled on the Steam Community Market. Gear moves both ways, so the grind has a price tag.                  FEATURES    Runs above your taskbar, plays while you work    Idle & offline progression    Multiple heroes, each with a full skill tree    4 difficulties × 3 acts × dozens of stages, 12+ biomes    Elite mini-bosses + towering Act bosses    9 loot rarities, sockets & sets    Forge (0→+15) & Terminal crafting    Asynchronous PVP, Daily Raid and a Top 100 ranking    Tradable Unique items on the Steam Community Market    Steam Achievements    WISHLIST NOW AND SURVIVE THE OUTBREAK

name: Game in Picture
lang: English
short: Game in Picture (GiP) is a desktop companion app that keeps your game visible in a picture-in-picture overlay when you Alt+Tab, with manual source controls, audio management, process freezing for single-player games, and customizable themes.
about: Game in Picture (GiP) is a picture-in-picture desktop companion app built for players who frequently switch contexts. Instead of losing awareness when you Alt+Tab, GiP keeps a live view of your game visible in a compact overlay so you never miss the action. With manual source controls, audio management, process freezing for single-player games, and customizable themes, GiP makes interruptions less punishing and helps you return to the action faster with fewer missed moments.   Your game, your rules!         GiP is designed for games running in Borderless Fullscreen (also known as Windowed Fullscreen).   Four ways GiP can help  GiP keeps your game within reach when you step away from full-screen play.            Pause When You Need To   Pause and resume supported single-player or offline games directly from GiP when you need to step away. Auto-pause can be enabled separately for each game, allowing GiP to pause it when you leave fullscreen and resume it when you return. Before pausing software with online capabilities or active network traffic, GiP displays a warning so you can decide whether it is safe to continue.  GiP does not modify memory or touch save data. It does not rely on the game’s built-in pause system. Instead, it temporarily suspends the game process, freezing the game exactly where it is, even if the game has no pause function of its own.        Media and Audio Controls in One Place   Control the tracked application’s sound without opening the Windows volume mixer. Click the audio control to mute or unmute, then drag around it to adjust volume. Auto-mute can silence the tracked window whenever you switch away and restore its sound when you return. For recognized browsers and media players, GiP also provides play/pause and previous/next commands when the application supports them.         Manual Source Control   By default, GiP automatically follows the fullscreen window you Alt+Tab away from. When you want tighter control, Explicit Tracking only changes the source when you hold the backtick key while Alt+Tabbing, while Manual Selection lets you choose a specific eligible window from the source list.   Manual Mode   Choose exactly which window GiP follows whenever you want direct control. Switch between your game, a browser, a guide, a video, or another app without rebuilding your overlay, then keep the selected source visible over the fullscreen application you are using.   Pin Mode   Keep GiP visible over fullscreen windows. Move between fullscreen apps while GiP shows the window you switched away from; when using Manual Source Control, your selected source remains fixed.         Themes and Visual Style   Match GiP to the rest of your setup with a selection of visual themes. Each theme updates the interface consistently while preserving clear controls and readable information across different games and desktop environments.         Flexible Overlay Placement   Resize and position GiP to suit your screen, game, and workspace. Keep the overlay locked in a corner, move it wherever it avoids important on-screen information, or use a compact floating layout that stays useful without taking over your display.         Expanded View Mode   Double-click GiP to switch between Normal View and Expanded View. Expanded View gives more of the window to the captured image and keeps surrounding interface elements out of the way. Move the pointer over GiP whenever you need its title bar or controls again. A separate Fullscreen option from the context menu can expand GiP across the entire display.         Tray Integration and Quick Access   Keep GiP available for long sessions without adding unnecessary desktop clutter. Send it to the system tray when it is not needed, restore it quickly, and use convenient tray actions to reach common controls and capture options.

Monsters keep walking in, your party holds the line, and your heroes level up on their own.          A guild worth running  Hire heroes at the Tavern, field the party your way and keep the rest in Reserve. Merge two and the survivor always gains a skill, sometimes a new rarity. about: Welcome to Astral Forge: Desktop Alchemist.    On your desktop while you work, back to the workshop when you play   Everyday computer use can help prepare your next alchemy experiment. Typing, mouse movement, idle time and time online contribute to different resources.  Carry on working, studying or browsing. When you have a moment, return to stoke the fire, cool the furnace, forge items, sort your discoveries or see what other alchemists have sent.   Choose how your workshop runs   Desktop wallpaper mode: keep the workshop beneath your Windows desktop icons and other applications.  Windowed or full-screen display: open it like a regular game to focus on alchemy, collections and trading.  Energy-saving mode: enable the power-saving settings for longer sessions and adjust background frame rate and rendering resolution as needed.  For a break from the keyboard and mouse, start a 25-minute meditation at the pool and collect the corresponding materials when you finish.           Set the temperature and see what this batch brings   Add fire to raise the furnace temperature or water to lower it, then choose when to forge. Temperature affects the result; the item's quality and affixes give you more to investigate after the reveal.  Identify unknown items, try combining or reforging them, or dismantle unwanted finds to recover resources for another attempt. Sometimes you get ordinary materials; sometimes a discovery worth keeping.           Build a collection of your own   Fill your compendium, from everyday items to rare relics, and look for affix combinations you like.  Organize and expand your inventory, make room for new finds, and display eligible collectibles in the workshop. Chase a better item or work towards those entries you have yet to unlock.           Exchange discoveries with other alchemists   Exchange supplies through trading ships, send or receive messages in bottles, and use item trading and auctions to find what you need.  These interactions are asynchronous: no real-time multiplayer room or matching schedules are required. Develop your own workshop, exchange resources when you need to and occasionally receive another player's discovery.   Give your resources more uses   Resource exchanges, an in-game bank, trading and auctions let you prepare materials, manage your game currency and rearrange your collection.  From inventory expansion to long-term investments involving wonders and the colossus, decide whether to keep crafting, complete your collection or save for the next goal.           Watch for workshop surprises   Occasional events need your attention. A bomb that suddenly appears, for example, calls for a timely response.  Alongside alchemy and collecting, remember to check what is happening in the workshop.           Take rare collectibles into your Steam Inventory   Eligible special items can be exported to your Steam Inventory. Items that support market trading can be traded on the Steam Community Market.  Item eligibility, an in-game license and Steam's trading and market rules apply. The license can be unlocked using game resources or obtained earlier through payment. Buying the game and obtaining the license are separate.        Internet connection   Internet required.   Gameplay and features   Astral Forge: Desktop Alchemist combines a fantasy alchemy workshop with desktop companionship, idle progression and incremental growth. Desktop wallpaper mode, windowed and full-screen display, and energy-saving settings let it accompany everyday computer use. Keyboard input, mouse movement, idle time and online time contribute to resources.  Play includes temperature control, alchemy, forging, combining, identification, random affixes, reforging, dismantling, rare relic collecting, a collection compendium, displays and inventory expansion. short: A tiny monster-taming auto-battler that lives in the corner of your screen, and they never stop grinding. Catch 90 Minimon, build busted team comps, and rake in loot while you work, browse, or play something else entirely. They battle. You profit.
about: Collect ’Em, Train ’Em, Let ’Em Battle               Tiny Monsters. Big Numbers. Zero Downtime.   Catch Minimon, kit them out with loot, pick your upgrades, and let them brawl through wave after wave of enemies, all in a window small enough to live beside your spreadsheet, your browser, or that other game you're supposedly playing. Let them cook, or lock in and play hands-on. And when your squad finally hits a wall? Don't wait it out, swap gear, retool abilities, rebuild your strategy, and come back swinging.            Just don't get comfortable: the wave director is watching. It reshuffles enemy squads and load outs as you climb, so no two runs play the same.  Yesterday's unstoppable build might be today's rebuilding project. Think you can master all 9 elemental types and catch all 90 Minimon?   Assemble a Roster Worth Bragging About            Every Minimon you catch brings its own strengths, role, and build potential. But nobody rides the bench for free. Each member of your roster feeds passive stat bonuses to your active team based on its elemental type, so every single catch makes your whole squad stronger. Train your favorites, evolve them, and hunt for team combos that feel slightly unfair.   Craft Builds That Break the Game          Level up to unlock new Abilities: offensive, defensive, and utility. Curate each Minimon's kit into something that's uniquely yours. Stack the right pieces into a specialized build and there's no challenge you can't out-think.   Evolve, Loot, Repeat          Evolution isn't just a glow-up. Evolved Minimon gain extra ability slots and beefier stats, opening up whole new build possibilities. Mix and match gear to find your optimal setup, and unlock additional item slots to squeeze every last drop of power out of your team.    No Minimon Left Idle           Off-duty doesn't mean off the clock. Send benched Minimon on passive Adventures to haul back rewards and resources while you do... literally anything else. Clear Paths to earn Progress Points, then cash them in for permanent upgrades that make your entire roster stronger... forever!   Raids, 15 Paths, and a Mode That Never Ends    Raids are the proving ground: assemble a team of 3 Minimon and throw them into short, brutal battles against our toughest foes for our biggest rewards. Sloppy team-building need not apply.  Conquer any of the 15 unique Paths and you'll unlock Endless Mode, where the waves keep coming, the difficulty keeps climbing, and only one question matters... how far can you push?   Wishlist Minimon    Wishlist Minimon: Tiny Idle Tactics and follow along as we build toward launch. Grab the free Demo to play the first three levels right now. Your future squad is waiting.

short: A free-to-play hack-and-slash that fights on in your taskbar. Chibi heroes meet the enemy inside a thin strip at the bottom of your screen. All you do is swap the gear they picked up and respec their skills when you feel like it. No connection needed; the rest happens in the corner of your screen.
about: A hack-and-slash that fights on in your taskbar Chibi heroes meet the enemy inside a thin strip. They kill it, gear drops, the next one comes. It runs whether you touch it or not. When you feel like it, open the dashboard and swap what fell. That is all there is to it.        Free to play The base game is free. It will not be pay to win. There are no ads. No connection needed. It runs the same either way. There is no server, and no account to create. Pull the plug and nothing changes. No "servers are down today," and no day when the service ends and your save stops working. Yokai leak onto your desktop Now and then the ward slips and one gets out. It steps off the strip, walks the edge of your taskbar, and wanders across your desktop. Click it and it leaves something behind. Ignore it and it finds its own way back.        Anywhere you want it, any size you want    Thin enough to sit over your taskbar — and you can put it anywhere else on screen too    You can resize it. Tuck it small into a corner, or blow it up and watch    Multiple monitors? Drag it across them    The dashboard opens only when you want it. Combat keeps going while it is closed         Melt it. Forge it. Link it. Ten equipment slots: Main Weapon, Sub Weapon, Helm, Body Armor, Bracers, Greaves, two Rings, Amulet and Charm. What rolls on them is random. Nothing you pick up goes to waste.     Salvage  — break gear you don't want down into materials. Hang the right ema and low-rarity drops melt down the moment they fall, without ever touching your bag     Craft  — forge new gear from what you saved. What comes out is not left to chance     Link  — slot magatama (red for Might, blue for Arts, green for Life, yellow for Fortune) into your gear. Three of the same color and rank fuse into one of the next rank. Slotting and unslotting are free. Out of sockets? Drill more at the forge      One stat is never enough Cut your attack interval and it means nothing if each hit is light. Raise your crit rate and it means nothing while your crit damage stays where it was. Stack HP and you still fall if the incoming damage outpaces it. Power here shows up only when two or more things that are insufficient alone start meshing. Your gear screen always shows three totals —  DPS, Sustain and Power . That is where you find out what isn't meshing. Three layers decide your build     The Scroll (skill tree)  — a fork at every milestone: sharpen a skill, or change how it behaves. Widen your reach, or narrow it to a point. At the checkpoints on Lv10 and Lv25 you pick one of three branches. Respec is always free     Devotion (Ema)  — permanent upgrades bought with Merit, earned once for every stage you clear for the first time: experience, drop rates, inventory space, skill slots, even new party members. Whatever you buy keeps working forever     Vessels  — keep a character deployed and fighting, and the passive that belongs to them alone wakes up in stages   Vessels — hand a woken passive to someone else Once a character's vessel wakes, they can lend a copy of that passive to one other character. The owner loses nothing by lending it. Whose vessel goes to whom? You can raise a character on the bench and send nothing but their vessel to the front. Once your three are picked, there is still a layer left to build. Sigils — what the late game is about Only Legendary gear carries a unique effect. That is its sigil, shown as a single kanji. Finding a Legendary stops being the goal. Finding the one with the sigil you want takes its place. A sigil you like can be pulled out of the gear, recorded, and imprinted onto something else. Bosses Every area ends with the thing that rules it. Mid-bosses turn up along the way, and a key opens the door to something else.        COMBO Every kill pushes your COMBO up; stop killing and it decays. While it climbs, the gear that drops gets better and the enemies themselves spawn faster. The better your party meshes, the faster the fighting in the corn

name: Tillow
lang: English, German, French, Italian, Spanish - Spain, Portuguese - Brazil, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Russian, Spanish - Latin America, Turkish
short: Tillow is a cozy isometric farm builder that keeps working while you do. Lay out fields, keep animals, make your own wine or distil grappa, and let your workers take over. Docked as a narrow bar at the edge of your screen, it keeps you company while you do other things. No losing, no timers.
about: Tillow is an isometric farm builder. A river valley lies overgrown in front of you, and you turn it into your farm one piece at a time. You clear, plough, sow and harvest, until the first workers arrive and take the chores off your hands. You see your progress whenever you look across the valley.          From wild grass to wheat  In the beginning you pull every tuft of grass yourself. The wild grass buys you your first crop, wheat, and a little later you hire your first worker. From then on the farm runs. Fields join into groups that keep their sowing plan, workers sow and harvest, the harvest goes straight to your barn, and the market sells whatever you do not want to keep. You decide what grows next, and where.          At the edge of your screen  Tillow does not have to fill your screen. Switch to bar mode and the game becomes a narrow bar at the edge of your desktop, at the bottom, top, left or right, wherever you drag it. The farm keeps working there while you do, and nothing steals your attention. When you glance at it, you can tell at once whether there is something to do or to decide. Leave the bar open for a few hours and months have passed on the farm. When you have time again, pull the bar open and you are back in full screen.          Three farms, three valleys  Each farm sits in a valley of its own, with its own climate and its own character. You start in the floodplain, between half-timbered houses and mixed forest. The olive hill is warmer and Mediterranean, with vines and olives. The moor farm is cool and peaty, built from natural stone, with room for the herds. All three farms run at the same time: they share one purse, research together and ship goods to each other.                  What grows, and what it becomes  Grain and vegetables, orchards and vines, each with its own window in the year. Cows, sheep, pigs and poultry live out on the pasture and raise their young. From what the farm gives you, you make more: flour, cheese, honey, spirits, and wine that matures in the barrel cellar and carries its vintage year. All of it opens up through research, and some of it you only come across out in the valley.          Four seasons  In spring the seed comes up and the treetops blossom. In summer the fields stand full, and cloud shadows drift across the valley. In autumn the leaves turn, and the grape harvest begins. In winter there is snow on the roofs and ice on the river, and you build and research. Whatever you leave standing in autumn goes to seed and comes back next year.

short: A tiny food alley that sits quietly at the bottom of your screen. Customers wander in, take a seat, eat, pay up, and head back out. Get the ingredients in place and the alley runs itself — while you work, while you watch something.
about: A little alley appears at the bottom of your screen  Start it up and a small window settles in along the bottom of your screen. It won't jump in front of you, won't ping you with notifications.  It's just there. While you work, while you watch something, the alley gets through its day all on its own.    A customer comes walking up.  Stops right in front of an eatery they like, opens the door, slips inside and takes a seat.  When the dish comes out they dig in, pay up, and head back out looking pleased with themselves.  Meanwhile morning turns to afternoon, the sun goes down, night rolls in. And the alley is still right there.    More and more to look at     15 eateries  — start with a little toast stand and work up to cafes, burgers, ramen, pizza, sushi, curry, dumplings, pancakes.     45 dishes  — every eatery has its own cooking, and every customer has their own favorite     18 kinds of customers  — each with their own regular haunt and their own budget.     Morning to night  — the alley changes color with the hour, and so does who walks by      If you feel like digging deeper  The whole alley shares  one 8x8 pantry . Every ingredient for every eatery comes out of that one place.  And if something runs out? The customer just sits there and waits. Forever. That seat is tied up until you sort it out.    Where to put your  54 ingredients  — once you start seeing which eatery eats what, and how fast, the answer shows up     20 wisps  to summon — place one in the pantry and it works on every ingredient within its range. Finding where those ranges overlap is the best part    Unlock more slots, open more eateries, and redo your layout — grow your alley and find the setup that works best.  Your alley runs just fine on its own. But a smart setup makes it noticeably faster.      A good fit if you    like keeping something cute running in the corner of your screen    want an idle game without the endless clicking    enjoy staring at numbers until a layout falls into place      Good to know    Time only passes while the game is running. There's no offline progress.    Fully single-player. No connection, no account needed.    Saves sync through Steam Cloud.

short: A relaxing idle-aquarium garden simulator that sits at the bottom of your screen while you do other things.
about: AquaCorner is a transparent desktop aquarium idle game that runs as a living overlay on your screen. Not a separate window. Not a browser tab. It lives alongside everything else — always on, always thriving, and growing more vibrant the more you focus.             Your Fish Do the Work   Fish choose their own planting spots, sow their preferred species, and tend the foliage as it grows — all on their own. name: FISH OS
lang: English
short: An idle fishing game that lives inside a fake 1997 operating system. Click the water to fish, then run your catch through a desktop where every window is a mechanic: an aquarium that buffs your income, a fish market, a fleet you send out overnight. 250 species. Solitaire included.
about: FISH.OS is an idle fishing game built inside a fake operating system from 1997. You fish, sell the catch, upgrade your gear, buy boats that keep working while you're gone, and reset everything for a multiplier once the numbers get silly. It also comes with a card game, a paint program and a music player, since that's what used to ship on the disc.         Every system is a window. Open the fishing app and drag it wherever you want, keep the market running next to it, and leave the aquarium bubbling away in the back. You can arrange the desktop however you like or minimize the whole operating system, and the fish keep biting either way.         Every fish gets a pixel-art entry in the Fishpedia, sorted by rarity and by the zone it lives in. Common fish fill the log quickly and the rare tiers take a long time. You can fuse duplicates into hybrids, show off your best catches in an aquarium you decorate yourself, and push the completion percentage up a decimal at a time.                 Buy boats, send them out on expeditions and let the fish in your tank earn for you. When you come back the next day there's a full balance waiting and a report on everything the fleet brought in overnight. Offline earnings are there from your first boat, and you never pay extra for them.         Compact mode docks FISH.OS along the bottom of your screen, right above the taskbar, with the water, your boats and the catch dial. Fish bite and boats go by while you do something else, and one click lands the catch. Expand it again whenever you want the full desktop back.              Formatting the drive wipes your progress and gives you a permanent multiplier. Build better rods in the workshop, crack rocks for materials in the lab, unlock new fishing zones and earn titles along the way, and each run gets you further than the last.         FISH.OS comes with Solitaire, FishSweeper, Fish 2048, a paint program with layers and TunaPlayer for music, plus desktop themes, a screensaver and a seagull, and every one of them works.                       Catch 250 species across unlockable zones    Run an economy of boats, upgrades and offline expeditions    Prestige for permanent multipliers and deeper runs    Decorate an aquarium and fill out the Fishpedia    Host or join a co-op session and fish with friends    Play the bundled 90s software, all of it working    Music from real West Coast bands    Dock it to the bottom of your screen and keep fishing while you work

about: Start with nothing—aim to become a millionaire.  Even while you’re working on your PC, Lily keeps working away in the corner of your desktop.  This game is a desktop-resident idle game set in the turbulent city of “GRIT City.”  Lily starts out with almost nothing—no coins and no job.  Whether working at a construction site, delivering pizzas, cleaning the streets, or working as a security guard… she’ll take on various jobs to collect coins and aim for 1,000,000 coins.  The basics of the game are very simple.  Use “WORK” to earn coins.  When you get tired, take a break with “REST.”  Once you’ve finished the day’s work, move on to the next day.  Since the game can be left running in the corner of your screen, you can enjoy it while doing your usual PC activities—like working, studying, or watching videos.  From small jobs to big dreams!  At first, you can only do simple jobs.  However, as you collect Coins and grow, new jobs and new areas of the city will gradually unlock.  Construction sites, pizza delivery, security, office work…  What kind of job will you take on today to collect Coins?  In this city, you never know what might happen.  It’s not just about working.  Suddenly, you might get attacked by a stray dog.  WOOF! -5 Coins  Or you might get a tip from a customer.  NICE TIP! +5 Coins  You might chase thieves, break tools, pick up a wallet, or even get caught up in strange, inexplicable events.  There are good times and there are terrible times.  Enjoy these unpredictable random events.  Work, rest, and rise to the top.  As you collect Coins, your character’s life will gradually change.  Starting with nothing, she gradually becomes more prosperous as she continues working.  There’s only one goal.  1,000,000 Coins  Whether you’re working, studying, or just relaxing and watching videos,  in the corner of your desktop, she’s living her life today.    Work. Rest. Get Rich.  And try not to get bitten by a dog.
